html:
The Royal Naval Dockyard on Ireland Island, Bermuda, was built from 1809 as Britain's main base in the western Atlantic. Britain needed it after losing its ports in the American Revolution.

Much of the heavy stone work was done by convicts shipped from Britain and Ireland, held in prison hulks in the harbour. From here the Royal Navy raided Washington and Chesapeake Bay in the War of 1812.

The dockyard served through both world wars and closed in 1951. Its fortress, the Keep, is now the National Museum of Bermuda, and the old buildings serve cruise ships. Bermuda's long naval link with London helps explain its loyalty to the crown today.
